summary: The STOP Nitazenes Act amends the Controlled Substances Act to permanently place 2-benzylbenzimidazole opioids, commonly known as nitazenes, into Schedule I. It defines specific chemical structures and names several individual substances belonging to this class, removes their temporary status if they were previously scheduled temporarily, and directs the Attorney General to issue implementing rules.

affected_groups.effect: Must issue rules to implement the Act within one year and is authorized to publish lists of qualifying substances in the Federal Register and issue interim final rules.
Subject to permanent Schedule I controlled substance restrictions and requirements for any materials, compounds, mixtures, or preparations containing 2-benzylbenzimidazole opioids.

key_provisions: Permanently adds 2-benzylbenzimidazole opioids (nitazenes) to Schedule I of the Controlled Substances Act.
Provides chemical structure criteria detailing modifications at various positions, including the 1-position, 2-position, the benzimidazole ring phenyl portion, and the 6-position.

Includes specific substances under the definition, such as Etonitazene, clonitazene, metonitazene, isotonitazene, protonitazene, butonitazene, etodesnitazene, flunitazene, N-pyrrolidino etonitazene, N-desethyl isotonitazene, and N-piperidinyl etonitazene.
Grants the Attorney General the authority to publish by order in the Federal Register a list of substances satisfying the definition.
Removes the temporary scheduling status for any included substances, making them permanently subject to Schedule I requirements upon enactment.
Requires the Attorney General to issue implementing rules within one year of enactment, which may be issued as an interim final rule.

summary_detail.significance: The bill permanently classifies a specific class of synthetic opioids as Schedule I controlled substances under federal law, replacing or solidifying any temporary scheduling status and directing regulatory enforcement and rule issuance by the Attorney General.
